programme: RBPJ is the DNA-binding effector of Notch signalling (its own target set contains NOTCH1, NOTCH3, HES1, HEY1, HEY2, LFNG — a canonical Notch cassette) and is documented to control endothelial-pericyte communication and vascular remodeling (Apelin/Cdc42) when lost. ETV4 (PEA3-family ETS factor) drives an MMP/urokinase-plasminogen programme (MMP1/2/7/13/14, PLAU, PLAUR, TIMP1, CXCL8, CAV1) that supplies the matrix-remodeling proteases vessels need to sprout or tumours need to invade. COPS5 (JAB1/COP9 signalosome) sits on CDKN1B and VEGFA, the classic p27-degradation/HIF-VEGFA angiogenic switch. Together these three name a vascular remodeling / angiogenesis module: Notch sets vessel-wall identity and stability, COPS5 sets the HIF-VEGFA drive, ETV4 supplies the proteolytic remodeling.
role_in_a: In Kidney_Clear_Cell_Carcinoma this module underwrites the tumour's defining hypervascular, invasive phenotype: ETV4 sits at strong Open Targets association (0.95 percentile) and its MMP/PLAU target set matches the invasion/ECM-degradation biology ETV4 is known for in RCC; COPS5's VEGFA/CDKN1B targets fit the VHL-loss-driven HIF-VEGFA angiogenic switch typical of ccRCC. RBPJ itself is only weakly associated here (0.33 percentile, no literature retrieved), so its contribution in kidney is inferred from the shared programme rather than independently evidenced.
role_in_b: In Stroke this module maps onto cerebrovascular integrity and post-ischemic repair: RBPJ carries the strongest signal (0.90 percentile, and three retrieved papers show Rbpj loss disrupts vascular remodeling via Apelin/Cdc42 and impairs endothelial-pericyte communication — the same axis disturbed in small-vessel disease). ETV4 is placed in stroke by one paper, but through a distinct mechanism (restraining YBX1-GPX4 ferroptosis in ischemia-reperfusion), not through its MMP/invasion targets. COPS5's stroke association is weak (0.049 percentile, no direct paper).
shared_axis: Both diseases are, at bottom, vessel-behaviour disorders: ccRCC is among the most vascularized solid tumours, built on HIF-VEGFA drive and protease-mediated invasion, while stroke is fundamentally a failure of cerebrovascular perfusion and integrity, with Notch-pericyte-endothelial signalling governing vessel stability and repair. The same angiogenesis/remodeling toolkit (HIF-VEGFA via COPS5, ECM turnover via ETV4, vessel-wall identity via RBPJ/Notch) would be redeployed in a growing tumour's neovasculature and in an ischemic brain's damaged and repairing vasculature.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors' own target genes (Notch cassette under RBPJ, MMP/PLAU under ETV4, VEGFA/CDKN1B under COPS5), and each disease independently places at least one carrying factor strongly (ETV4/COPS5-relevant genes score high in ccRCC; RBPJ scores high in stroke with three mechanistic papers). But no retrieved source connects ccRCC and stroke through this axis directly — the link rests on reasoning about shared vascular biology, not a documented pair-specific fact — and ETV4's one stroke paper works through ferroptosis, a different mechanism from the invasion programme that justifies its inclusion, which weakens the story's internal consistency.
support: PMID 37051908 — Rbpj deficiency disrupts vascular remodeling via abnormal Apelin and Cdc42 signalling, directly tying RBPJ to cerebrovascular remodeling. PMID 36147294 — pathological pericyte expansion and impaired endothelial cell-pericyte communication under endothelial Notch loss, the same pericyte-endothelial axis relevant to small-vessel stroke pathology. PMID 39890825 — CNS resident macrophages show region-specific immunogenic states under Rbpj deficiency, an immune (not strictly vascular) facet of the same Notch loss. PMID 42304629 — ETV4 restrains YBX1-GPX4 ferroptosis cascades to improve cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, placing ETV4 in stroke but via a mechanism distinct from its MMP/PLAU target set.
how_to_falsify: In matched ccRCC tumour-endothelium and post-ischemic cerebral cortex samples, ChIP-seq/ATAC for RBPJ and ETV4 at their MMP/Notch target loci: if the bound target repertoire is not shared (e.g., ETV4 binds MMP/PLAU loci in kidney but binds an entirely non-overlapping ferroptosis-related gene set in ischemic brain, with no shared vascular targets), the claim of one shared angiogenesis/remodeling module is falsified in favor of tissue-specific repurposing of the same factors for unrelated processes. A supporting check: RBPJ or Notch-pathway inhibition (e.g., gamma-secretase blockade) should reduce both ccRCC tumour vascular density/invasion and worsen post-stroke pericyte-endothelial coupling if the same programme is truly operative in both.
caveats: Support ranges from 18/45 to 30/45 patient-group comparisons across these factors — recurrent but not universal — over 4 independent cohort pairs. The tissue pairing is blood|kidney: stroke-side expression almost certainly comes from blood/PBMCs, not brain tissue, so the cerebrovascular story for RBPJ is imported from external literature on Rbpj-deficient vascular models, not observed directly in the retrieved expression data; RBPJ's own target list also includes immune/NF-kB genes (CD40, FOXP3, TRAF2, NFKBIA, FCRL5), consistent with Notch's independent role in blood-lineage immune differentiation, so some of its signal may reflect immune rather than vascular biology. Excluded tissue-generic factors (SPI1, CEBPB, GFI1, JUNB — myeloid/immune master regulators) confirm the retained signal is not simply generic blood-immune-cell activity. None of the single-view exclusions (MXD4, TEAD4, TAF1, NR2E3, NFATC3, POU3F4, NCOA2, NAB2, HMBOX1, NHLH2, ZNF32) offer an alternative vascular or Notch-adjacent candidate, so the module is not an artifact of a dropped better-fitting factor. NCOR2 and ELF3 both carry strong ccRCC association but were left out of the programme because their target sets (nuclear-receptor corepression; epithelial differentiation) do not mechanistically fit a vascular-remodeling story.
